facts.text: Fishhook sits in Alaska's Matanuska Valley, where gently rolling hills were carved by glaciers and shaped by the active Castle Mountain Fault.
The area’s lowest points lie around 800‑1,000 feet, while peaks rise above 6,000 feet, creating diverse microclimates across Fishhook.
Fishhook experiences a subarctic climate, with cool summers and cold, snowy winters, thanks to its 61.7°N latitude.
Covering about 65 square miles, Fishhook boasts several lakes and the Little Susitna River, offering a rural backdrop.
Outdoor enthusiasts head to Fishhook for hiking, skiing, and biking in the nearby Government Peak and Hatcher Pass state recreation areas.
Fishhook should not be mixed up with the earlier community of the same name, now called Chalkyitsik.
